title: Embed prefill coalescer and kernel-autotune to cut p99 tail
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: reduce embedding endpoint P99 tail by addressing ingress microbursting, cold-kernel penalty, and per-tenant variance. We will implement a lightweight prefill coalescer in the ingress path that buffers very short windows (1-6ms) to allow opportunistic microbatches, introduce a kernel-autotune pass that selects kernel variants based on short-run fingerprinted sequence length histograms, and add KV-cache prewarm heuristics for reranking workflows. This ticket drives experiments, implementation, and rollout for a safe canary with rollback metrics. Motivations: recent on-call pages and benchmarks show large p99 spikes during tenant ingress bursts and after autoscale events. Reducing p99 improves SLA adherence for Dedicated customers and reduces cost from wasted kernel cold-starts.
acceptance_criteria: P99 end-to-end latency for embeddings API reduced by >=50% on synthetic burst workload (baseline p99 420ms -> <=210ms)
No degradation of p50/p95 beyond 5% across measured tenants during 72h canary
Kernel selection autotune has safe fallback (previous kernel) and logs decisions to perf trace
Canary rollout with throttled traffic and automatic rollback if p99 increases by >10%
Documented config flags for prefill coalescer hysteresis and per-tenant opt-out
work_notes: 2025-02-11 - Spike & hypothesis: observed p99 jumps correlated with ingress bursts and kernel cold-path executions. Collected flamegraphs and per-kernel timings from 2025-02-05..2025-02-09.

2025-02-14 - Prototype prefill coalescer added to staging ingress. Buffer window 4ms by default, max buffered requests 16. Initial microbatching logic implemented in C++ fast-path with lock-free queue.

2025-02-18 - Kernel-autotune prototype: offline profiler collects histogram of sequence lengths per tenant over 10k requests and recommends top-2 kernel variants. Implemented selection shim in runtime that prefers recommended kernel for next 1000 inferences.

2025-02-21 - Experiment A: baseline burst test using synthetic trace (1000 reqs/s bursts). Results: baseline p99 420ms -> prefill coalescer only p99 240ms (43% reduction). p50 unchanged. Memory overhead <2% per worker.

2025-02-24 - Experiment B: prefill coalescer + kernel-autotune + KV prewarm for reranking workflows. Results: p99 420ms -> 110ms (74% reduction) on reranking-heavy trace. Noted small increase in p95 for long sequences (+6%).

2025-02-26 - GA decision meeting: enable prefill coalescer by default, kernel-autotune opt-in for dedicated and private customers for first rollout. Agreed to add per-tenant telemetry and opt-out flag.
2025-02-28 - Safety work: added fallback path when autotune kernel yields >10% latency regression over 5-minute window. Added tracing tags to correlate kernel switch events with QoS metrics.
2025-03-02 - Canary started on 5% traffic for runtime-1.22 cluster in us-west-2. Early telemetry: p99 down 62% aggregated; two tenants showed +8% p95 — investigating sequence length skew.
2025-03-04 - Post-canary tweak: increased coalescer hysteresis for tenants with high variance and add tenant-level min-buffer threshold to avoid extra latency on ultra-low-latency SLAs.
2025-03-04 - Next: roll out to 25% with monitoring, complete runbook, and prepare release notes and SDK compatibility notes.
experiments: exp-2025-02-21-INGRESS-BURST: synthetic bursts (1k rps for 30s, cooldown 60s). prefill window 4ms, max batch 16. p99 420->240ms.
exp-2025-02-24-RERANK-WORKLOAD: mixed long/short sequences, KV prewarm enabled, kernel autotune candidate set {kv-optimized, matmul-fused}. p99 420->110ms, p95 +6% for long seqs.
exp-2025-03-02-CANARY: live traffic 5% across 12 tenants. aggregated p99 -62%, two tenants flagged for sequence skew.
decisions: Enable prefill coalescer by default for hosted API and Dedicated; offer tenant-level opt-out for latency-sensitive customers.
Kernel-autotune will run offline every 6 hours to propose candidate kernels and apply changes with a short probationary window and rollback on regression.
KV-cache prewarm heuristic: for reranking endpoints, if tenant shows repeated near-identical prefixes, send a speculative prewarm to reduce first-token penalty.
Avoid aggressive batching for tenants with SLA p50 < 10ms by adding per-tenant minimum-exempt flag.
next_steps: Extend telemetry mappings so that kernel-switch events are surfaceable in Console per-route dashboard
Run 72h stability on 25% rollout and verify p95/p99 across geos
Finalize PR to add config UI in Console for per-tenant coalescer settings
Prepare engineering runbook and on-call playbook for autotune regressions
